judged_text: The only authorization for overwriting any user's app credentials is a single static shared secret sent verbatim in a header — no HMAC, no timestamp, no nonce, no per-user scoping, no rate limit on the route — and the decrypted keys blob is JSON.parse'd and written to credential.key with no schema validation. Anyone who obtains the two static secrets (which .env.example instructs operators to share with the parent application) can silently replace any user's OAuth tokens with attacker-chosen tokens (e.g., redirecting a victim's booking/event data to attacker calendars), a captured request can be replayed forever to roll a re-authed user back to stale credentials, and a buggy parent app stores malformed keys with a 200 response.

adjudication.rationale: The new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` authorizes credential overwrite solely by comparing a request header to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (no HMAC/signature, timestamp/nonce, or per-user scoping) and then allows writing credentials for any `userId` in the body after decryption. It decrypts `reqBody.keys` and does `JSON.parse(...)` and directly persists the resulting object into `prisma.credential.update/create` as `key` with no schema validation of the decrypted payload. This enables anyone with the static secret(s) to replace arbitrary users' stored OAuth credentials and makes replay/rollback feasible because there is no freshness check in the handler.
